body:
It seems this is more problematic than I expected.

The fundamental problem is that we rely solely on the `JPH::BodyID` for overlap lookups in `JoltArea3D`, which can be different for the same body even when the `RID` isn't, since we actually destroy and re-create the `JPH::Body` as it gets removed from and added back into the physics space.

The only solution I can see would be to have `JoltArea3D::body_shape_entered` and `JoltArea3D::area_shape_entered` check all the other overlaps to see if there's another one with the same `RID` that has a `pending_removed` for the same `JPH::SubShapeID` pair, and then reconcile the two somehow.

I really don't like the idea of having to iterate all the overlaps though.

We also can't just switch `bodies_by_id` to use the `RID` as key, since the body could have been freed at that point, and the only thing we would get from the contact listener is the destroyed `JPH::BodyID`.

I guess a separate hash map specifically for `RID`-to-`Overlap*` lookup could be a thing, but that also seems unfortunate, especially for what is arguably a rare edge-case.

@jrouwe I'd be curious to hear your take on this, and if you see some better way of solving it.

To clarify, the expected behavior here is for `Area3D::_body_enter_tree` to emit the `body_entered` signals and such, and then the side effects from the body having been removed and re-added would cancel eachother out in some way (or not happen at all, ideally), which means no further signals are emitted.

I don't know exactly what the rules are for bodies vs spaces. I assume a body can exist in only 1 space and most likely that space is not know during `JoltBody3D` construction. Possibly, bodies can be transferred from space to space.

In any case, depending on the rules, you could perhaps construct a `Body` instead of a `BodyCreationSettings` from the beginning (on the default space?) and keep that body around when it's removed from the space (so removing but not destroying it). Only when transferring a body to a different space you would need to destroy and recreate it. That way its body ID would remain consistent during the entire lifetime. It would also mean that you can simplify a lot of setters that either apply their change to `jolt_settings` or `jolt_body` to always apply to `jolt_body`.

A simpler change could be to keep the `jolt_settings` vs `jolt_body` distinction, but to keep `jolt_body` around after removing it from a space (as a kind of cache). This would mean that on re-insert, you need to check if the space is the same and if it is, reapply all settings from `jolt_settings` to `jolt_body` before inserting into the physics system. If it is a different space, you'd destroy the body and create a new one.

> I don't know exactly what the rules are for bodies vs spaces. I assume a body can exist in only 1 space and most likely that space is not know during `JoltBody3D` construction. Possibly, bodies can be transferred from space to space.

Yes to all of those.

> you could perhaps construct a `Body` instead of a `BodyCreationSettings` from the beginning (on the default space?)

There isn't really any notion of a default space (and thus no default `JPH::PhysicsSystem`) from the physics server point of view, unfortunately. We could maybe create one, but I'm not sure how wasteful that is, and I guess more importantly, would a `JPH::Body` allocated from one `JPH::PhysicsSystem` be able to keep the same `JPH::BodyID` in whatever other `JPH::PhysicsSystem` it gets moved to? If yes, is there some risk of conflicts there? I must admit I haven't really taken the time to understand all the properties of `JPH::BodyID`.

> keep `jolt_body` around after removing it from a space (as a kind of cache)

I haven't pondered all the edge-cases, but that does actually sound fairly straight-forward. My only concern there would be what the cost is of keeping a `JPH::Body` around. Is it purely the memory of the class itself? If someone were to remove some "root" node (e.g. a level) from the scene tree that contained a lot of areas for example, but didn't actually free those nodes, we would now be keeping all those `JPH::Body` instances around indefinitely.

We could probably solve that with yet another `SelfList`, where objects register to have their `JPH::Body` destroyed, and which would get processed at the physics step, much like `JoltSpace3D::needs_optimization_list`. Then we would remove the object from that list if it were to ~~re-enter the same space again~~ enter a space again.

> would a JPH::Body allocated from one JPH::PhysicsSystem be able to keep the same JPH::BodyID in whatever other JPH::PhysicsSystem it gets moved to?

No, unless you do very careful `BodyID` management. In practice this would be very wasteful as 'max bodies' (as specified in `PhysicsSystem::Init`) would need to be `<number of spaces>` times as high. I would expect though that if you remove a body from one space and insert it in the next that you get an exit and enter message, so I don't think `BodyID`s need to be consistent across spaces.

> My only concern there would be what the cost is of keeping a JPH::Body around. Is it purely the memory of the class itself?

A `Body` + its `MotionProperties` counterpart is 320 bytes in a single precision build, so the memory is not that bad. But a `Body` that you keep allocated does count towards the 'max bodies' limit.

Looking at the interface again, I realize there is a solution that uses less memory. Instead of using `BodyInterface::DestroyBody` I could make a new function similar to `BodyInterface::UnassignBodyID` that retains the `BodyID` instead of recycling it. You could then use `BodyInterface::DestroyBodyWithoutID` to delete the `Body` object. You can store the `BodyID` in e.g. `JoltBody3D` and when you construct a new `Body` you would call `BodyInterface::CreateBodyWithID` instead of `BodyInterface::CreateBody` to reuse it. The `BodyID` you keep still counts towards the 'max bodies' limit but you don't keep any memory for the `Body` lying around (so the cost is effectively 4 bytes for the `BodyID`). Also, since a `BodyID` belongs to a `PhysicsSystem` you would need to destroy the `BodyID` when switching spaces.

You could indeed combine this with the `SelfList` idea to recycle `BodyIDs` after a physics step.

Funnily enough I was just about to put up a pull request that uses `UnassignBodyID` and `DestroyBodyWithoutID` to recycle the `JPH::BodyID`, but at the point where the body gets added to a new space, so not quite as elegant as what you're describing. You can see my attempt [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...mihe:godot:jolt/reuse-body-ids).

I did not consider that this actually spends your body limit though, which is less than ideal.

I ran into some problems with the `SelfList` stuff though, which is why that's not in there, but now that I'm sitting here typing up an explanation for why I think I just managed to rubberduck myself into a potential fix for said problems.
Note that UnassignBodyID makes the ID available for other bodies. You don't maintain ownership of that ID. The name I chose is a bit misleading. I would need to create a new function.

`CreateBodyWithID` is called right after, so there shouldn't be any opportunity for any other body to claim it, unless I'm misunderstanding something.

It was mostly just a way to be able to still use `jolt_settings` without having to manually assign its properties over to the recycled body.

I just pushed a revised version (to the [branch](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...mihe:godot:jolt/reuse-body-ids) mentioned above) that adds the `SelfList` deferred destruction. This means that if a body/area is pulled out of the scene tree and then left there until the physics step then the `JPH::Body` will be destroyed automatically, unlike before where I just let it hang around. So while it's still a bit wasteful to have the full `JPH::Body` hang around until that time, I'm much less concerned about the memory overhead now.

One compromise with this approach is that if you move a body through spaces A->B->C->A within a single physics frame you'll still get the weird events, but I can't imagine anyone would actually do this.

The max bodies stuff you mentioned is concerning though. I assume this means that if you pull out some massive level branch out of the scene tree, containing half of the max bodies amount, and then add another massive level branch to the scene tree, containing another half of the max bodies amount, you'll end up hitting the limit and trigger the error, despite seemingly keeping under the limit.

That would technically be a breaking change I guess, although the fix would be simple, and is arguably communicated clearly in the existing warning.

> Is placebo because both the `if` and `else` path are identical in functionality.

I had a feeling that might be the case.

> In that case, maybe I should add a specific helper function for that.

As in something like `Body::Assign(const BodyCreationSettings &inSettings)`? That would probably work, yeah.

> Correct, although you could also start destructing bodies from the `SelfList` if you run out of bodies (with as an obscure side effect that you reintroduce the possibilty for this bug in that specific context).

Oh right, of course. That should be easy enough I guess.
